sub_field_roles: King of Sonitpur, Devotee of Shiva
key_achievements: Mighty ruler of ancient Sonitpur; central figure in the Hari-Hara war and father of Princess Usha whose romance with Aniruddha is commemorated in the legend of Agnigarh.

sub_field_roles: King of Pragjyotisha, Warrior King, Commander
key_achievements: Legendary king of Pragjyotisha renowned in the Mahabharata; commanded an army of Kiratas and Chinas on his formidable elephant Supratika during the Kurukshetra War.
Expanded Kamarupa's sovereignty across northern Bengal (Pundravardhana) and performed the Vedic Ashwamedha (horse sacrifice) to signify imperial supremacy.

sub_field_roles: King of Kamarupa, Diplomat, Patron of Learning
key_achievements: Greatest monarch of the Varman dynasty; formed a historic alliance with Emperor Harshavardhana of Kannauj; hosted Chinese scholar-monk Xuanzang (Hiuen Tsang); established Kamarupa as a premier center of scholarship.
notable_works_titles: Nidhanpur Copperplates, Doobi Plates, Patron to Nalanda University

key_achievements: Founded the historical Varman Dynasty of Kamarupa, bringing the region into the documented epigraphic era of Indian history; contemporary of Gupta Emperor Samudragupta.
Issued the earliest dated inscription found in Assam (Tezpur Rock Inscription, 829 CE) establishing riverine navigation and dispute regulations on the Brahmaputra; excavated the Harjjar Pukhuri lake.
notable_works_titles: Tezpur Rock Inscription (829 CE), Harjjar Pukhuri

key_achievements: Established the Salastambha dynasty of Kamarupa with Haruppeshwara (near modern Tezpur) as the royal capital following the decline of the Varmans.
Rebuilt the grand temple of Hataka Sulin (Lord Shiva) in Haruppeshwara; issued the Tezpur and Parbatiya copperplates detailing royal administration and temple endowments.

sub_field_roles: Founder King of Kamarupa Pala Dynasty
key_achievements: Elected by the citizens and nobles of Kamarupa to re-establish stable royal lineage after the extinction of the Salastambha line; founded the Pala Dynasty of Kamarupa.
Renowned scholar-king who composed exquisite Sanskrit verses preserved in his royal copperplates; founded the city of Kamarupanagara.
Fortified the capital city Durjaya with impenetrable ramparts along the Brahmaputra; expanded copper mining, metallurgy, and Vedic scholarship in Kamarupa.
Author of the opening song in the Charyapada (*Ka'a tarubara pancha bi dala*), the earliest surviving corpus of Eastern Indo-Aryan / proto-Assamese poetic and mystic literature.
First of the 84 Mahasiddhas in Buddhist Tantra and foundational guru of the Nath yogic tradition; traditionally linked with ancient Kamarupa and the fishermen community of the Brahmaputra.

Legendary folk sage born in Lehidangara near Barpeta; creator of *Dakor Bachan* (Sayings of Dak), an invaluable ancient oral encyclopaedia of agriculture, weather forecasting, astrology, dietetics, and social ethics.
Peerless statesman, diplomat, and military commander during the Mughal-Ahom conflicts; rallied the state alongside Lachit Borphukan; author of one of the finest Buranjis.

dynasty_movement_org: Ahom Dynasty (Reign of Chakradhwaj & Udayaditya Singha)
key_achievements: Legendary general who decisively defeated the massive imperial Mughal armada led by Ram Singh I at the **Battle of Saraighat (1671)**; immortalized for his dictum *'My uncle is not greater than my motherland'*. National Defence Academy awards its best cadet the Lachit Borphukan Gold Medal.

sub_field_roles: Reigning Queen Regnant (Bor Raja), Patron of Education
key_achievements: First woman to formally reign as supreme monarch (*Bor Raja*) of Assam; established the first institutional Sanskrit and girls' schools in the capital; issued Persian-inscribed royal coinage.
notable_works_titles: Gaurisagar Tank & Temples, Establishment of Girls' Schools

sub_field_roles: Founder King of the Ahom Kingdom, State-Builder
key_achievements: Led the historic Tai-Ahom migration across the Patkai hills in 1228 CE; established his capital at Charaideo; unified diverse ethnic tribes (Morans, Borahis, Kacharis) into the composite Assamese socio-cultural identity (*Bor Asom*). Celebrated on Assam Day (Asom Divas, Dec 2).
notable_works_titles: Establishment of Charaideo Capital, Buranji Chronicle Tradition

key_achievements: Decisively expelled the Mughal Empire from Assam forever at the **Battle of Itakhuli (1682)**, fixing the western boundary at the Manas River; re-established internal stability after decades of political turmoil.
notable_works_titles: Battle of Itakhuli (1682), Umananda Temple Construction

sub_field_roles: First Barbarua, Chief Minister, Urban Planner
key_achievements: Mastermind of the Ahom administrative and village socioeconomic structure; codified the Paik system; organized self-sufficient Assamese model villages (*Paik Bor-Khel*); father of Lachit Borphukan and Laluksola Borphukan.
notable_works_titles: Codification of Paik System & Village Planning

key_achievements: Heroic Ahom warrior woman who took up arms and led troops against the invading Bengal Sultanate general Turbak Khan in 1532 to avenge her martyred husband Borgohain Phrasenmung.

Instituted the foundational **Paik System** and Khel reorganization under minister Momai Tamuli Barbarua; created the posts of Borphukan (viceroy of Lower Assam) and Barbarua; built fortifications and defeated Mughal invasions.
notable_works_titles: Reorganization of Paik System, Creation of Borphukan & Barbarua Offices

dynasty_movement_org: Ahom Dynasty (Reign of Gaurinath & Kamaleswar Singha)
key_achievements: Statesman who governed Assam during the devastating Moamoria Rebellions; modernized the Ahom army with disciplined standing troops armed with flintlock muskets; held the state together for over 35 years.
notable_works_titles: Suppression of Moamoria Uprising, Military Modernization

sub_field_roles: Swargadeo, Architect, Patron of Arts & Sports
key_achievements: Transformed the Ahom empire into its golden architectural age; built the new brick metropolis of Rangpur, the grand Joysagar Tank & Temples, Namdang Stone Bridge, and institutionalized Rongali Bihu and indigenous sports at court.
notable_works_titles: Founding of Rangpur Capital, Joysagar Tank, Namdang Stone Bridge

key_achievements: Endured brutal physical torture for 14 days at Jerenga Pathar by the puppet boy-king Lora Raja without revealing the hideout of her fugitive husband Prince Gadapani (later King Gadadhar Singha), saving the future of Assam.
notable_works_titles: Martyrdom at Jerenga Pathar (1680), Joy Sagar Tank commemoration

key_achievements: Brought significant Brahminical cultural and administrative synthesis into the Ahom court; shifted capital to Charguya; established Singarigharutha coronation ritual.

One of the greatest Ahom monarchs; annexed the Chutia kingdom; repulsed multiple Bengal Sultanate invasions (Turbak Khan); introduced firearms/cannon technology to Assam; created the high office of Barpatragohain; first Ahom king to take the Hindu title *Swarganarayan*.
notable_works_titles: Creation of Barpatragohain post, Introduction of Saka Era in Buranjis

key_achievements: Unmatched military commander known as *Chilarai* (Kite-like lightning general) for his lightning amphibious assaults; conquered multiple regional states; devout Vaishnavite scholar who authored Sanskrit commentaries (*Saravati*). Bir Chilarai Divas celebrated across Assam.
notable_works_titles: Saravati (Sanskrit Commentary on Gita Govinda), Chilarai Divas

key_achievements: United the indigenous Koch, Mech, and tribal chieftaincies of Western Assam/North Bengal into the powerful Koch Kingdom; revived the sacred Kamakhya shrine pilgrimage.

Presided over the golden age of Western Assam; rebuilt the magnificent Kamakhya Temple in 1565; granted royal refuge and grand patronage to Srimanta Sankardev and Madhavdev, enabling the Bhakti literature and Sattriya renaissance.
notable_works_titles: Reconstruction of Kamakhya Temple (1565), Patron to Sankardev

sub_field_roles: Last Queen of Chutia Dynasty, Warrior Queen
key_achievements: Fierce queen who organized female archers and resistance against invading forces; chose heroic self-sacrifice by jumping from Chandragiri hill rather than surrender her dignity. Sati Sadhani Divas observed on April 21.
notable_works_titles: Defense of Chandragiri / Sati Sadhani Divas

sub_field_roles: King of Chutia Dynasty, State Builder
key_achievements: Consolidated the Chutia kingdom in northeastern Assam; forged diplomatic relations with Gauda; patronized trade and riverine fortifications across Sadiya.

sub_field_roles: Vaishnavite Guru, Founder of Brahma Samhati
key_achievements: Prominent religious reformer and contemporary of Sankardev; founded the influential Patbausi and Vaikunthapur Sattras and the Brahma Samhati branch of Assamese Vaishnavism.

sub_field_roles: Vaishnavite Preceptor, Founder of Haridevi (Brahma) Samhati
key_achievements: Founded the Maneri Sattra; key figure in spreading Bhakti philosophy across Western and Central Assam.

sub_field_roles: Chief Disciple of Sankardev, Saint-Poet, Playwright, Musician
key_achievements: Chief successor to Sankardev; author of the immortal *Naam Ghosha* (Book of Psalms); established the iconic Barpeta Sattra; composed sublime Borgeets, Jhumuras, and Ankiya Nats.
notable_works_titles: Naam Ghosha (নাম ঘোষা), Bhakti Ratnavali, Borgeet, Arjuna Bhanjana (Jhumura)

sub_field_roles: Polymath, Saint-Reformer, Poet, Playwright, Painter, Musician, Social Philosopher
key_achievements: Supreme cultural icon of Assam; founded the egalitarian Ekasarana Harinama Dharma; created Sattriya dance (one of India's 8 classical dance forms), Borgeet (classical music), Ankiya Nat (one-act drama), Brajavali literary idiom, and the community socio-democratic institution of the **Namghar**.
notable_works_titles: Kirtana Ghosha, Chihna Yatra (1468), Bhagavata Purana translations, Rukmini Harana, Borgeet, Gunamala

key_achievements: One of the earliest documented Assamese poets; composed *Prahlada Charitra* and *Hara Gauri Samvada* under the patronage of King Durlabhnarayan of Kamata.
notable_works_titles: Prahlada Charitra (প্ৰহ্লাদ চৰিত), Hara Gauri Samvada

key_achievements: Composed the *Saptakanda Ramayana* into colloquial Assamese verse—the earliest vernacular rendering of Valmiki's Ramayana in any modern Indo-Aryan language in North/Eastern India; acknowledged by Sankardev as the unassailable *'Purba Kavi'* (predecessor poet).

sub_field_roles: Court Poet of Koch King Naranarayan
key_achievements: Rendered the epic Mahabharata into Assamese (comprising over 30,000 verses), incorporating indigenous folk ballads and Vadha-Kavyas (*Bhim Charit*); court poet of King Naranarayan and Chilarai.
notable_works_titles: Assamese Mahabharata, Bhim Charit (ভীম চৰিত), Baghasur Vadha

sub_field_roles: Vaishnavite Reformer, Founder of Mayamara Sattra
key_achievements: Founded the Mayamara Sattra and the egalitarian Kala Samhati tradition; initiated widespread conversion of tribal communities (Morans, Chutias) on principles of absolute social equality without caste discrimination.
notable_works_titles: Founding of Mayamara Sattra, Puranjan Akhyana

name_english: Hazrat Shah Miran (Ajan Fakir / Ajan Pir)
key_achievements: Baghdad-born Sufi mystic who settled in Gorgaon/Saraguri Chapori; composed soul-stirring **Zikir and Zari** spiritual devotional songs blending Islamic mystic teachings with Assamese folk meters; immortalized communal harmony in Assam.

sub_field_roles: Father of Assamese Prose, Sanskrit Scholar
key_achievements: Hailed as the **Father of Assamese Prose**; wrote *Katha Gita* and *Katha Bhagavata* in the 16th century, establishing Assamese as one of the earliest Indian vernacular languages to develop sophisticated formal philosophical prose.
notable_works_titles: Katha Gita (কথা গীতা), Katha Bhagavata (কথা ভাগৱত), Bhakti Viveka

dynasty_movement_org: Ahom Court (Reign of Siva Singha & Ambika Devi)
key_achievements: Authored the monumental illustrated elephant veterinary encyclopaedia **Hastividyarnava** in 1734 CE on Sanchi bark manuscript, illuminated by court painters Dilbar and Dosai.

notable_works_titles: Featured on Wikipedia: Badan Chandra Borphukan

key_achievements: Pioneer of modern Assamese intellectual consciousness; submitted the historic memorandum to British Commissioner A.J. Moffatt Mills in 1853 demanding the reinstatement of the Assamese language in colonial courts and schools.
notable_works_titles: A Few Remarks on the Assamese Language (1855), Asamiya Lorar Mitra

key_achievements: Compiled the magnum opus **Hemkosh** (1900), the authoritative etymological dictionary that standardized modern Assamese spelling and grammar; crusaded against untouchability, opium addiction, and social evils in pioneering plays like *Kaniyar Kirtan*.
notable_works_titles: Hemkosh (হেমকোষ), Asamiya Bhasar Byakaran, Kaniyar Kirtan, Bahire Rongsong Bhitore Kowabhaturi

key_achievements: Pioneered modern realistic Assamese social drama with *Ram-Navami* (1857) advocating widow remarriage; authored the comprehensive *Assam Buranji* (1884) and the definitive biography of Anandaram Dhekial Phukan.
notable_works_titles: Ram-Navami (ৰাম-নৱমী), Assam Buranji (1884), Anandaram Dhekial Phukanar Jiwan Charitra

key_achievements: Compiled and published the **first Assamese-English Dictionary** in 1867 (*A Dictionary in Assamese and English*) with 14,000 words; instrumental in getting Assamese restored as the official court and school language in 1873.
notable_works_titles: A Dictionary in Assamese and English (1867)

key_achievements: Founded and edited **Orunodoi** (1846), the first Assamese news magazine/periodical; fought against British policy replacing Assamese with Bengali; established the modern Assamese printing press at Sibsagar.
notable_works_titles: Orunodoi (অৰুণোদই, 1846), Grammatical Notices of the Asamese Language (1848)

sub_field_roles: First Assamese ICS Officer, World-Renowned Sanskrit Grammarian, Barrister
key_achievements: First graduate from Assam (Calcutta University), first Assamese to crack the prestigious ICS exam in London (1870), and first Assamese Barrister; published monumental 3-volume English-Sanskrit Dictionary and grammatical treatises praised by Max Müller.
notable_works_titles: Practical English-Sanskrit Dictionary (3 Vols), Higher Sanskrit Grammar, Mahaviracharita critical edition

key_achievements: Pioneered the modern Assamese sonnet (*Priyotamar Chithi*); compiled the mammoth *Asamiya Sahityar Chaneki* (Typographical Selections from Assamese Literature, Calcutta University); recovered and preserved rare ancient Buranjis and manuscripts.
notable_works_titles: Priyotamar Chithi (1st Assamese Sonnet), Asamiya Sahityar Chaneki, Phular Chaki

dynasty_movement_org: Jonaki / Asamiya Bhasha Unnati Sadhini Sabha / Asomiya
key_achievements: Founder, financier, and first editor of the epoch-making journal **Jonaki** (1889) in Calcutta; inaugurated the Romantic movement in Assamese poetry with *Bonkuwori*; founder of *Asomiya* newspaper.
notable_works_titles: Pratima (প্ৰতিমা), Bin-boragi, Bonkuwori (1st Assamese Romantic Poem)

sub_field_roles: Doyen of Modern Assamese Literature, Satirist, Playwright, Folklorist
key_achievements: Foremost architect of modern Assamese literature; composed the state anthem of Assam *'O Mur Apunar Desh'*; compiled beloved folk fairy tales *Burhi Aair Sadhu*; edited *Bahi*; created the immortal satirical persona Kripabar Borbarua; presided over the 7th Asam Sahitya Sabha.
notable_works_titles: O Mur Apunar Desh (State Anthem), Burhi Aair Sadhu (বুঢ়ী আইৰ সাধু), Kripabor Borbaruar Kakotor Tupula, Belimar, Jaymati Kunwari

sub_field_roles: First President of Asam Sahitya Sabha, Novelist, Dramatist, Editor
key_achievements: Elected the monumental First President of the **Asam Sahitya Sabha** at Sibsagar in 1917; authored early novels like *Bhanumoti* (1890) and *Lahori*; edited influential periodicals *Usha* and *Assam Banti*.
notable_works_titles: Bhanumoti (ভানুমতী), Lahori, Sri Krishna, Joymati, Lachit Borphukan

dynasty_movement_org: Earle Law College / Modern Assamese Prose
key_achievements: Master of thoughtful, aphoristic Assamese prose; authored authoritative grammar *Bahal Byakaran* and moral philosophical essay collections *Sarathi* and *Chintamoni*.

sub_field_roles: Historian, Executive Councillor, President of Asam Sahitya Sabha
key_achievements: Authored the seminal historiographical work **Early History of Kamarupa (1933)**; founded and edited the Journal of the Assam Research Society (JARS); established the Assam Provincial Museum.
notable_works_titles: Early History of Kamarupa (1933), Foundation of Assam Museum

sub_field_roles: Historian, Biographer, President of Asam Sahitya Sabha
key_achievements: Renowned historian of the Ahom era and 1857 uprising in Assam; author of classic biography of Maniram Dewan; won Sahitya Akademi Award (1960 for *Kongressar Kanchiyoli Rodot*); awarded Padma Bhushan (1983).
notable_works_titles: Maniram Dewan (মণিৰাম দেৱান), Kongressar Kanchiyoli Rodot (Sahitya Akademi 1960), Satawoli

key_achievements: Established the scientific historical evolution of the Assamese language in his groundbreaking doctoral dissertation **Assamese: Its Formation and Development (1941)**; pioneer of modern Assamese literary criticism and Tantric-Vaishnavite cultural studies.
notable_works_titles: Assamese: Its Formation and Development (1941), The Mother Goddess Kamakhya, Kalita Jatir Itibritta, Purani Asamiya Sahitya

sub_field_roles: Scholar, Art Historian, Lexicographer, President of Asam Sahitya Sabha
dynasty_movement_org: Gauhati University / Punjabi University (Saint Kabir Chair)
key_achievements: Monumental indologist and cultural historian who systematically documented and presented the Sankardev heritage and Sattriya traditions to global academia; author of *Early History of the Vaisnava Faith and Movement in Assam*; awarded Padma Shri (1972) and Sangeet Natak Akademi Fellowship.
notable_works_titles: Early History of the Vaisnava Faith and Movement in Assam (1965), Prachya Sasanavali, Asamiya Sahityar Ruprekha

sub_field_roles: Barrister, President of Assam Pradesh Congress, Orator
dynasty_movement_org: Swaraj Party / Indian National Congress / Pandu Congress (1926)
key_achievements: Foremost national leader who brought Assam into the mainstream of the Non-Cooperation and Swarajist movements; successfully organized the historic 41st Indian National Congress Session at Pandu (Guwahati) in 1926; president of Asam Sahitya Sabha (1927).
notable_works_titles: Leadership of 1926 Pandu Congress, Shikari (Hunter stories)

sub_field_roles: General Secretary of Assam Pradesh Congress, Lyricist, Lawyer
key_achievements: Visionary nationalist leader and orator who gave up his lucrative legal career for the Non-Cooperation movement; authored patriotic songs and translated Shakespeare into Assamese.
notable_works_titles: Sasthi, Tarun Kanchan, Translation of Hamlet (Bhimdorpo)

sub_field_roles: Ahom Prince, First Anti-British Rebel Leader
key_achievements: First leader in Assam to raise the banner of armed revolt against British East India Company rule in 1828; declared himself Swargadeo at Borphukanar Khat and marched on Rangpur.
notable_works_titles: 1828 Armed Revolt against East India Company

key_achievements: Led the earliest organized anti-British rebellion in Assam in 1830; attempted to blow up the British ammunition magazine at Rangpur; hanged by the colonial regime in 1830.

sub_field_roles: First Indian Commercial Tea Planter, Revolutionary Martyr
key_achievements: First indigenous commercial tea planter in India (Chenidhora and Cinnamara estates); masterminded the 1857 uprising in Assam to overthrow British colonial rule and restore the native Ahom monarchy; executed by hanging on February 26, 1858 in Jorhat.
notable_works_titles: Establishment of Cinnamara Tea Estate, 1857 Revolt leadership in Assam

key_achievements: Elderly nationalist woman who struck British Captain Finish with the national flag staff when he insulted the Indian tricolour during the Barhampur Congress office reoccupation on September 18, 1942; succumbed to bullet wounds.

sub_field_roles: Youth Leader, Mrityu Bahini Freedom Fighter
key_achievements: 17-year-old fearless freedom fighter who led the unarmed procession of the *Mrityu Bahini* (Death Squad) to hoist the Indian National Flag at the Gohpur police station on September 20, 1942; shot dead by British police while holding the Tricolour high.
Martyred alongside Kanaklata Barua on September 20, 1942 when he grabbed the fallen Tricolour from Kanaklata's hands and was fatally shot by British forces.

dynasty_movement_org: Indian National Congress / Quit India Movement
key_achievements: The **only martyr in the entire country to be hanged by the British in the Quit India Movement of 1942** (falsely implicated in the Sarupathar military train derailment); embraced the gallows with serene Gandhian courage at Jorhat Jail on June 15, 1943.

sub_field_roles: Freedom Fighter, Poet, Journalist, Social Crusader
dynasty_movement_org: Asom Jatiya Mahasabha / Chetana & Deka Asom
key_achievements: Fiery nationalist poet and revolutionary; established the *Asom Jatiya Mahasabha* and *Asom Songrakkhini Sabha* to protect indigenous rights and culture; founded *Chetana* and *Deka Asom* periodicals; Sahitya Akademi Award (1965).
notable_works_titles: Tumi, Anubhuti (অনুভূতি), Bandookar Guli, Bedanar Ulka

sub_field_roles: Feminist Pioneer, Social Crusader, Author, Freedom Fighter
dynasty_movement_org: Asom Pradeshik Mahila Samiti (1926) / Quit India Movement
key_achievements: Founding mother of the women's rights movement in Assam; established the historic **Asom Pradeshik Mahila Samiti** in 1926; fought against child marriage, caste oppression, and purdah system; active leader in Non-Cooperation and Civil Disobedience movements. Awarded Padma Shri (1972).
notable_works_titles: Founding of Asom Pradeshik Mahila Samiti, Pitribhita (Novel), Asomiya Chora

sub_field_roles: Second Chief Minister of Assam, Governor of Madras (Tamil Nadu)
dynasty_movement_org: Government of Assam / Government of India
key_achievements: Known as the *Iron Man of Assam* (Lauhamanab) for his uncompromising integrity, strong border security policies, industrialization initiatives, and panchayati raj empowerment; served with great distinction as Governor of Tamil Nadu.
notable_works_titles: Chief Minister of Assam (1950–1957), Governor of Madras (1958–1964)

sub_field_roles: First Chief Minister (Premier) of Assam, Constituent Assembly Member
key_achievements: Architect of Modern Assam; saved Assam from inclusion in East Pakistan under the Cabinet Mission Grouping Scheme with Mahatma Gandhi's backing; founded Gauhati University, Assam Medical College, Guwahati High Court; posthumously awarded **Bharat Ratna (1999)**.
notable_works_titles: Saving Assam from Grouping Clause (1946), Drafting Sixth Schedule of Constitution, Bharat Ratna (1999)

sub_field_roles: Member of Parliament (Lok Sabha), Principal of B. Barooah College, Travelogue Writer
dynasty_movement_org: Praja Socialist Party (PSP) / B. Barooah College
key_achievements: Stalwart parliamentarian acclaimed in the Lok Sabha for brilliant debates on border defense and national integration; author of classic travelogues (*Mekong Nai Dekhisu*) and *The Red River and the Blue Hill*.
notable_works_titles: The Red River and the Blue Hill, Mekong Nai Dekhisu, Sagar Dekhisa

sub_field_roles: 5th President of India, Union Cabinet Minister, Advocate
dynasty_movement_org: Government of India / Indian National Congress
key_achievements: Prominent freedom fighter and advocate from Assam who served as Union Cabinet Minister across key ministries (Food & Agriculture, Petroleum) and was elected the **5th President of India (1974–1977)**.
notable_works_titles: 5th President of the Republic of India (1974–1977)

sub_field_roles: Chief Minister of Assam, Peace Negotiator
key_achievements: Longest serving Chief Minister of undivided Assam (1957–1970); established the historic Nagaland Peace Mission alongside Rev. Michael Scott and Jayaprakash Narayan; constructed the Saraighat Bridge and oil refineries; awarded Padma Vibhushan (1971).
notable_works_titles: Nagaland Peace Mission (1964), Saraighat Bridge inauguration (1962), Padma Vibhushan (1971)

sub_field_roles: Music Composer, Sattriya Exponent, Actor, Freedom Fighter, Marxist Leader
dynasty_movement_org: Revolutionary Communist Party of India (RCPI) / IPTA
key_achievements: Conferred the revered title **Kalaguru** by Kashi Hindu University (Varanasi) for his peerless Tandava dance exposition; unifier of diverse indigenous Assamese ethnic folk traditions; composed revolutionary and lyrical Rabha Sangeet; donated ancestral estates to landless peasants. Celebrated on Rabha Divas (June 20).
notable_works_titles: Rabha Sangeet (ৰাভা সংগীত), Asomiya Krishtir Somu Abhas, Siraj (Film), Sur-Setu

sub_field_roles: Father of Assamese Cinema, Playwright, Lyricist, Freedom Fighter
key_achievements: Directed **Joymoti (1935)**, the first Assamese and third Indian talkie film, overcoming monumental technical hurdles at Bholaguri Tea Estate; established the genre of **Jyoti Sangeet**; wrote pioneering modernist plays like *Sonit Kunwari* and *Karengar Ligiri*. Shilpi Divas celebrated on January 17.
notable_works_titles: Joymoti (1935, 1st Assamese Film), Indramalati (1939), Sonit Kunwari, Karengar Ligiri, Jyoti Sangeet

key_achievements: Known as *Natasurya* (Sun of Drama); starred in Assam's first film *Joymoti* (1935); wrote and directed immortal patriotic and social plays including *Siraj*, *Bhugjora*, and *Kiyaw*.
Known as *Geetikavi* (Lyric Poet) for his melancholic, nature-suffused songs and pastoral poetry; directed early Assamese film *Rupohi* (1941).

sub_field_roles: Queen of Goalpariya Lokageet, Folk Maestro
dynasty_movement_org: Gauripur Royal Family / Goalpariya Folk Tradition
key_achievements: Royal princess of Gauripur who elevated grassroots folk ballads of mahouts and cart-pullers to international acclaim; recorded evergreen classics like *'Hastir Kanya'*, *'Mur Mahut Bandhur Re'*; awarded Padma Shri (1991) and Sangeet Natak Akademi Award.
notable_works_titles: Hastir Kanya (হস্তীৰ কন্যা), Mur Mahut Bandhur Re, O Mor Hayre Doyamoy

sub_field_roles: King of Bihu, Folk Maestro, Composer
dynasty_movement_org: All India Radio / Sangeet Natak Akademi
key_achievements: Hailed as the *King of Bihu* (Bihu Samrat); transformed indigenous Bihu songs and Tokari Geet into quintessential cultural heritage across India; awarded Sangeet Natak Akademi Award (1992).
notable_works_titles: Kolore Patote Gai O Ronga Bou, Ma Ami Sodiya Looi Jam, Tokari Geet Collections

sub_field_roles: Music Maestro, Lyricist, Singer, Filmmaker, Poet, Humanitarian
dynasty_movement_org: Indian People's Theatre Association (IPTA) / Sangeet Natak Akademi
key_achievements: Colossus of Indian music whose songs of universal brotherhood, folk vitality, and riverine philosophy (*'Bistirno Parore'*, *'Manuhe Manuhor Babe'*) transcended linguistic barriers; Chairman of Sangeet Natak Akademi; recipient of **Bharat Ratna (2019)**, Dadasaheb Phalke Award (1992), Padma Vibhushan, Padma Bhushan, Padma Shri, and National Film Awards.
